thread_text:
oncall-bot: :warning: ALERT: gpu-node-42 triggered CUDA OOM despite 2GB headroom. Error spike observed on serving-runtime (inference) at 09:02 UTC. Auto-retry started. Marking for live triage.

maria: on it, taking lead. jumping into node.

aj: ack. scope? how many pods/nodes? any cross-region impact? :eyes:

oncall-bot: Observed: 6 failing requests/minute routed through node. Replica churn on 3 pods. Headroom metric shows ~2GB reserved but fragmentation metric > 78%.

kai: running quick check, attaching `nvidia-smi` snapshot:```nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
memory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB]
11032 MiB, 16384 MiB
```looks like free memory but allocation calls failing.

sanjay: sounds like fragmentation / reserved block mismatch. remember last-week pattern where KV cache reservation prevented contiguous allocs. check reserve slab/blocks and KV cache reclaim.

nina: any recent deploys to serving-runtime?

deploy-bot: Canary rolled 09:00 UTC: revision r-2026-03-14-09. No config changes to allocator flags.

aj: running diagnostics:```kubectl -n redwood logs pod/serve-abc-3 -c runtime | tail -n 50
E allocator: cuMemAlloc_v2 failed: out of memory
E runtime: failed to allocate contiguous block size=3.2GB
E runtime: reserve_available=2.0GB but max_contig_free=512MB
```Looks like headroom is fragmented. Also `dmesg` shows no host OOM.

maria: good catch. we're seeing contiguous allocation failures even though aggregate free > requested. try reclaiming KV cache and evicting lower priority replicas. I'll trigger KV cache flush on that node.

opsbot: running reclaim: `runtimectl kvcache flush --node gpu-node-42 --reason=oom-mitigation` -> started. Expect 10-20s to complete.

sanjay: parallel action: increase sparepool/evac buffer to allow more contiguous blocks. If runtime supports reserve adjustment, add 4GB to sparepool.

opsbot: `allocatorctl reserve --node gpu-node-42 --add 4GB --reason=emergency` -> returned OK, but note: this consumes cluster-wide free pool.

kai: after KV flush and reserve bump, attempt small allocation test from a debug pod:```python
# quick alloc probe
import cupy as cp
try:
  a = cp.empty((1024*1024*512//8,), dtype=cp.float32) # ~2GB
  print('alloc ok')
except Exception as e:
  print('alloc fail', e)
```probe returned alloc fail with cuMemAlloc_v2 despite reserve change.

support_lead: customer impact? any 5xxs or degraded latency feeding into support? we need ETA for mitigation to update status page.

oncall-bot: 5 customers reported request errors (500) in the last 12 minutes; error rate increased x12 for the affected routing key. No region-wide outage.

nina: copying CUDA stderr from pod:```E [2026-03-14T09:02:45Z] cuda:cuMemAlloc_v2 error: out of memory
stack: runtime::AllocContiguous() +0x1a4
... allocator: slab_free_count=324 slab_fragmentation_ratio=0.79
```

aj: hypothesis: headroom is in many small free chunks; allocator can't coalesce due to pinned reserved blocks (KV cache / long-lived sessions). Options: 1) force eviction of long-lived KV caches, 2) enable spill-to-host so runtime can satisfy allocs by paging hot KV to host, 3) restart offending pods to drop pinned allocations.

maria: do 1 and 2 first. I'll enable spill-to-host for node to allow transient allocations. This is risky for latency but prevents OOM.

opsbot: command: `runtimectl set --node gpu-node-42 spill_to_disk=true --ttl=15m --reason=oom-mitigation` -> applied. Monitor perf.

kai: enabling spill cleared a subset of failures; allocation probe now returns "alloc ok" for 2GB test. Real traffic still shows some 5xxs as the canary pods get rescheduled.

sanjay: long-term fix: need allocator compaction path. Short-term: schedule rolling restart of pods on that node to reallocate contiguous chunks. We'll cordon node and drain gracefully.

maria: initiating drain: `redwoodctl node cordon gpu-node-42 && redwoodctl node drain gpu-node-42 --evict-priority=low` -> draining 3 pods.

aj: grab pprof/heapprof for root cause:```curl http://serve-abc-3:6060/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap-serve-abc-3.pb
runtime-alloc-metrics:
  reserved_blocks: 32
  largest_contiguous_free: 512MB
  kvcache_pinned: 1.8GB
```save for postmortem.

support_lead: prepping customer comms. I'll post an initial status update: "We are mitigating elevated errors for a subset of inference requests in us-west. Temporary mitigations applied; no data loss. Engineers are performing rolling restarts. ETA 30-45m."

oncall-bot: action log: KV flush, reserve bump, spill-to-disk enabled, node cordon/drain initiated. Severity set to SEV2. Incident channel created #inc-memory-surge-3181234567.

kai: handing primary to @maria for live work; I'll take next 30m to monitor metrics and run heap diffs.

maria: handing to @kai at 09:40 UTC for second shift; my checklist: ensure draining completes, confirm no new 500s after drain, collect pprof and allocator dumps, escalate to infra-research if compaction fix needed.

sanjay: file a short-term ticket to add an allocator flag that forces compaction on demand: "allocator:force-compact --node". We'll schedule work in the infra backlog.

nina: note for postmortem: record that canary roll at 09:00 touched runtime revision r-2026-03-14-09 but config unchanged. Investigate whether runtime scheduling pattern increased fragmentation.

support_lead: we've posted status page and updated 5 affected customers via private channel. We'll send a follow-up once node is healthy and p99 latency is back to baseline.

oncall-bot: last update: drain completed at 09:31 UTC, pods rescheduled on other nodes, error rate back to baseline after 12:02 minutes. Spill-to-disk reverted at 09:36 UTC.

maria: closing live incident work; collecting artifacts into ticket INC-2026-743. I'll own the postmortem draft and assign root-cause analysis to @sanjay and allocator team.

sanjay: got it. will pull allocator traces and check if reserve accounting drifted.

kai: will upload pprof + heap dumps to shared folder and link in the ticket.

support_lead: thanks all. we'll do customer follow-up and ensure action items in postmortem. :white_check_mark:
